 November 15th: Sunday’s Nations League Accumulator – 5/1 Special, Betting Tips & Analysis
 With the Nations League action rolling onto Sunday, we are treated to another stacked schedule from across the continent.
 As the heavyweight trio of France, Italy and Belgium all look to punch their respective knockout stage tickets, there are plenty of eye-catching betting promotions available.
 For those of you looking to stick on a Sunday flutter, we have taken a glance at some of the most attractive Nations League accumulator tips.
 Sunday, November 15th 
 BST 14:00 Cyprus vs Montenegro 
 While some in Cyprus’ camp might have been left frustrated on Thursday evening as they were eventually forced to settle for a 1-1 stalemate away at Armenia, Akis Mantzios’ camp have enjoyed an eye-catching Nations League campaign this year.
 Sat firmly in the driving seat to follow Sunday’s opponents out of Group C this weekend, the Blues are unbeaten in all of their previous four consecutive Nations League appearances (two wins, two draws).
 Despite getting their League C adventure underway with a 2-1 loss at the hands of Montenegro on September 25th, Cyprus have come roaring back and are enjoying their most fruitful flurry in recent memory.
 Getting October underway with consecutive victories against Armenia and Latvia, Sunday’s hosts have also impressed with their recent success on home soil.
 In fact, Cyprus have won each of their last three straight appearances in front of their own supporters by an aggregate score of 7-3.
 Already cruising their way to a League B return and hardly having to get out of third-gear, Montenegro are in the midst of what has become a stellar purple patch.
 With the mood in Mirko Vucinic’s camp at a red-hot high, the Brave Falcons are riding a serious wave of momentum and will be looking to make a final Nations League statement on foreign soil.
 Last seen on Thursday clinching a 2-1 win at home against Latvia, Montenegro have mustered 13 points from their five Nations League appearances this year.
 Likewise, getting proceedings underway with that 2-1 victory against Cyprus back in September, the Reds have also impressed with their clinical performances in the final third.
 Signing off September with a rollercoaster 3-2 victory away at Armenia, Sunday’s guests have notched at least a pair of goals in five of their last six appearances across all competitions. 
 Betting Tip: Over 1.5 goals @ 2/5 1xBet 
 19:45 France vs Turkey  
 Suffering a maiden defeat under new boss Zinedine Zidane on Thursday night as they fell to a 3-1 loss away at fellow European heavyweights Italy, France are seeking an immediate Nations League response here.
 Excited to make a return to Paris this weekend, Les Bleus will still be fancying their chances of topping the table and punching their knockout stage ticket with a flurry on home soil.
 Missing out on the chance to claim a World Cup bronze medal finish in North America over the summer as they eventually slumped to a sensational 6-4 defeat against England on July 18th, France are searching for some recent defensive stability.
 Nevertheless, rightfully installed as a landslide contender in Paris this weekend, Zidane’s superstar squad still hold a fearsome reputation for their success in Paris.
 It should be highlighted, the former world champions have not suffered a single competitive defeat in front of their own supporters since back in September 2024.
 While new boss Sergen Yalcin might have only officially taken charge last month, the ex-Besiktas manager is more than aware that he has an almighty job on his hands.
 Although the Crescent Stars might have touched down in North America over the summer almost universally regarded as a genuine dark horse contender, Sunday’s guests endured a public World Cup crisis.
 Failing to book a knockout stage spot and limping their way home early, Turkey have embarked on an infamous Nations League nightmare and have already sacrificed their League A status with a whimper.
 Falling to a 2-1 defeat at home against Belgium on Thursday evening, Yalcin’s new squad have remarkably lost all of their five Nations League matchups this year by an aggregate score of 13-3.
 With their Nations League struggles underlined by a 3-0 drumming against Belgium when opening October, Turkey have unsurprisingly gained a reputation for their glaring defensive issues.
 Betting Tip: Michael Olise to score anytime @ 8/5 BetUS 
 19:45 Belgium vs Italy  
 While there might have been plenty of raised eyebrows across the continent over the summer following Mark van Bommel’s shock appointment, Belgium are certainly relishing life under the ex-Antwerp boss.
 Last seen on Thursday evening making an immediate return to winning ways as they clinched a 2-1 victory away at Turkey, Sunday’s hosts are sat in the driving seat to punch their Nations League knockout stage ticket.
 Getting their League A campaign underway with a famous 2-0 victory in Rome on September 25th, Belgium will be desperately seeking a repeat performance when they return to Brussels this weekend.
 However, signing off September’s extended interval with a 4-1 drumming against France, van Bommel’s new squad know the importance of finding some essential defensive grit.
 In fact, the Red Devils have failed to register back-to-back competitive clean sheets across all competitions over the past 13 months.
 Laying down an almighty marker at the San Siro on Thursday as they stormed their way to a stellar 3-1 win against France, Italy are enjoying quite the Nations League purple patch.
 Despite suffering more infamous World Cup qualifying heartbreak back in March, the former European champions appear to be getting a new era underway under Roberto Mancini’s guidance.
 Signing off September with a dominant 4-1 romp away at Turkey, the one-time Manchester City boss has seen his resurgent squad register 10 points from their previous four League A appearances.
 Nevertheless, despite opening their Nations League finale leading the chase at the top of the table, Italy are searching for their own defensive steel.
 It should be highlighted, Mancini’s high-flying squad have failed to register a single Nations League clean sheet in any of their five showdowns during this year’s tournament.
 Betting Tip: Both teams to score @ 8/11 1xBet 
 Our Sunday Nations League Accumulator:  
 Cyprus vs Montenegro – Over 1.5 goals 
 France vs Turkey – Michael Olise to score anytime 
 Belgium vs Italy – Both teams to score
